comments.body:
Implementation pushed for review: Gerrit change 2556 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2556 (commit afe5ecf43bc0, branch reb-3a02-mcp-schema).

The 41-property list was verified authoritatively rather than trusted: derived by running find_drift() with BASELINED_OMISSIONS monkeypatched empty. It matched exactly, no differences.

## AC1 — declared 39 of 41; 2 are permissive omissions WITH stated reasons (AC3)

- GateResultOut: all 5 declared (criteria_count, line_count, keyword_count, ac_items, file_impact).
- TicketStateOut: all 23 declared.
- NextBatchOut: 11 of 12. `tasks` is omitted with a reason — it belongs to the CLI-only `next-batch --limit=0` reduced variant (_engine_support/next_batch.py:559); the library/MCP path next_batch_state -> to_json_dict emits `batch` and never `tasks`.
- CreateResultOut: 0 of 1. `title` is omitted with a reason — only the CLI's `create --output json` emits it (_commands/composer.py:481); every MCP create tool returns rebar.create_ticket(return_alias=True), which builds {id, alias, description_warning, duplicate_warning} and drops title. Declaring it would advertise a permanently-null title on a ticket that always has one, and which the caller supplied as the tool argument.

## AC2 — BASELINED_OMISSIONS DELETED, not emptied

The dict, its comment block, and its merge line in find_drift are all removed. Grepping the gate for both `BASELINED_OMISSIONS` and `3a02` returns ZERO hits. `check_mcp_models --check` reports 'no missing declarations'.

## The non-obvious hazard this surfaced

Declaring an optional pydantic field makes it EMIT — and 15 of the newly declared properties have a canonical type admitting NO null (const: true, bare string, enum $ref, integer). A naive declaration therefore made real payloads VIOLATE THEIR OWN SCHEMA; 8 contract tests caught it (test_schema_ticket_state[mcp] and six test_canonical_tool_result_validates cases).

Fix: a new `_OmitUnsetOut` base with a model_serializer(mode='wrap') that pops a per-class _omit_when_unset tuple when the field was never set, modelled on the existing _HealthOut. **The emitted bytes are unchanged** while the declaration still appears in outputSchema. _HealthOut itself was deliberately NOT reused, because it would have suppressed the 9 already-declared defaults that _mcp_budget._wire_bytes documents as re-added.

Timestamps are typed `int | str | None`, never bare int: _mcp_errors.js_safe_result's docstring warns an int-declared field is coerced back to a lossy bare number on FastMCP re-validation (bug 6fe7). A regression test pins this.

## AC4 — wire-contract impact assessment

**All 39 newly declared fields were ALREADY on the wire** as undeclared extra='allow' pass-throughs. None is genuinely new data, so the change DOCUMENTS AN EXISTING SHAPE rather than altering it. Evidence: rebar.show_ticket() against this store's real ticket 3a02 returns 12 of the TicketStateOut fields today, and a union over 200 closed tickets adds 5 more; the remaining 6 are conditional reducer projections (_processors.py:121,186; _io/_provenance.py:56-58) that flow through extra='allow' identically whenever set. js_safe_result's docstring independently confirms it: 'TicketStateOut declares NO timestamp fields ... so created_at/updated_at pass through undeclared'. GateResultOut's 5 are returned on every return path of check_ac_compute / quality_check_compute (_engine_support/gates.py:64-79, 316-360). NextBatchOut's 11 are emitted unconditionally by to_json_dict (next_batch.py:331-373).

One caveat for the record: GateResultOut is ONE model serving TWO tools, so check_ac's outputSchema now advertises line_count etc. that check_ac never returns, and vice versa. The canonical gate_result.schema.json already had that shape, and _OmitUnsetOut keeps the runtime payloads disjoint exactly as before.

## A test that contradicted this ticket

F5 had added `test_the_baseline_names_its_tracking_ticket_and_is_not_open_ended`, asserting `'3a02-66ea-9229-470c' in source` — the exact OPPOSITE of AC2, which requires the baseline be deleted. It was removed and replaced with four tests: the baseline is gone rather than emptied, the four models cover their schemas minus only the documented omissions, every permissive omission is preceded by a reason comment, and the null-less-when-unset plus JS-safe-timestamp behaviours.

## Verification

check_mcp_models --check OK; drift heldout suite 17 passed; `pytest tests -k mcp` 801 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed; schema+budget+model+output sweep 1007 passed; make lint exit 0 (complexity new=0 increased=0, mechanism new=0 increased=0); make typecheck Success across 742 files. _mcp_models.py is 616 lines (was 508) against the 800 cap — 184 to spare, and no src/rebar file exceeds the cap.

comments.body:
Change 2556 review status: LLM-Review +1 (PASS, 1 advisory), but Verified -1 — AND THE CI FAILURE IS NOT THIS CHANGE'S.

The failing test is `tests/unit/test_bug_claim_rca_sequence_docs.py::test_claim_time_exemption_type_registry_includes_bug`, which touches none of this change's three files. It asserts a literal SOURCE STRING, `_PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES = ("bug"`, appears in src/rebar/_commands/gates.py.

I verified this is a MAIN breakage, not something 2556 introduced: checked out pristine origin/main into the worktree and ran the test there — 1 failed, 5 passed, identical assertion. It also fails identically on py3.11, py3.12 and py3.13, so it is deterministic, not flaky, and no recheck is warranted.

Root cause is a semantic merge conflict between two changes that were each green alone, which per-patchset CI structurally cannot catch: change 2544 added the source-text assertion, while change 2530 (mirror F3) consolidated that constant into rebar.types, so gates.py now imports it and the asserted literal no longer exists. No textual conflict, so Gerrit's Rebase-If-Necessary had nothing to flag.

Already owned and being fixed elsewhere: bug `5550-603c` (seaisland-deformed-shrike), in_progress and claimed by another session, with a fix pushed as Gerrit change 2557. I am NOT duplicating that work. 2556 will be rebased and re-triggered once 2557 lands.

The one advisory on 2556 is non-blocking: NextBatchOut's newly-added _omit_when_unset behaviour is untested. Worth addressing on the next patch set, since the equivalent behaviour for the other models IS covered.

## Context

Discovered while widening the MCP model/schema drift gate for mirror F5
(`62eb-5e6f-512a-420d`). That gate's registry covered 11 of 32 public `*Out` models. Deriving
the registry — every model whose `<snake_case>.schema.json` exists — brings 9 more models under
the check, and four of them are ALREADY DRIFTED.

## The measured gap: 41 undeclared schema properties

- **CreateResultOut** (create_result.schema.json) — 1: `title`
- **GateResultOut** (gate_result.schema.json) — 5: `ac_items`, `criteria_count`, `file_impact`, `keyword_count`, `line_count`
- **NextBatchOut** (next_batch.schema.json) — 12: `available_pool`, `batch`, `batch_size`, `epic_title`, `skipped_blocked`, `skipped_blocked_story`, `skipped_design_awaiting`, `skipped_in_progress`, `skipped_manual_awaiting`, `skipped_needs_planning`, `skipped_overlap`, `tasks`
- **TicketStateOut** (ticket_state.schema.json) — 23: `attestations`, `author`, `bridge_alerts`, `bridge_project`, `close_class`, `close_reason`, `completion_expectation`, `created_at`, `creation_channel`, `creation_channel_inferred`, `detected_by`, `env_id`, `force_close_reason`, `last_reopened_at`, `preconditions_summary`, `repos`, `reverts`, `source_author`, `source_created_at`, `source_env`, `source_id`, `updated_at`, `verify_commands`

## Why this is separate from F5

F5 fixes the GATE — it makes the check enum-aware and derives its registry so nothing can be
silently omitted again. Closing these 41 gaps is a different change with a different risk
profile: `_mcp_models` supplies the MCP tools' published `outputSchema`, so declaring a field
CHANGES THE WIRE CONTRACT clients read. That deserves its own review rather than riding along
inside a gate refactor.

F5 therefore baselines these four models as declared exceptions naming THIS ticket, so the gate
is green at rest while any NEW omission fails. Standard ratchet shape, the same one
`check_complexity_baseline.py` and `check_mechanism_delta.py` use.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: each of the four models declares the properties its canonical schema defines, or the
      schema is corrected where the property is genuinely not part of that payload. Verified by
      the drift gate reporting zero missing declarations for them with their baseline entries
      REMOVED.
- [x] AC2: the baseline exception entries added by F5 are deleted, not merely emptied, so the
      gate's exception map returns to naming only genuine permissive omissions. Verified by
      grepping the gate for this ticket id and finding none.
- [x] AC3: any property deliberately NOT declared carries a stated reason in the gate's
      permissive-omissions map. Verified by reading each remaining entry.
- [x] AC4 [non-codebase]: the wire-contract impact is stated — for each newly declared field,
      whether MCP clients could already observe it in practice. Verified by a comment on this
      ticket recording the assessment.

## Testing

- `python -m rebar.schemas.check_mcp_models --check` — zero drift with the baseline removed.
- `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_model_schema_drift_heldout.py -q`.

## Completion evidence (2026-09-03) — Gerrit change 2556 MERGED

- **AC1** — 39 of the 41 properties are declared on `CreateResultOut`, `GateResultOut`, `NextBatchOut` and `TicketStateOut`; the remaining 2 are permissive omissions with stated reasons (AC3). `python -m rebar.schemas.check_mcp_models --check` reports "MCP model schema drift gate OK — no missing declarations" with the baseline removed. The property list was derived authoritatively by running `find_drift()` with `BASELINED_OMISSIONS` monkeypatched empty, and matched exactly.
- **AC2** — `BASELINED_OMISSIONS` is DELETED, not emptied: the dict, its comment block, and its merge line in `find_drift` are all gone. `grep -c "BASELINED_OMISSIONS\|3a02" src/rebar/schemas/check_mcp_models.py` returns **0**.
- **AC3** — two deliberate omissions, each with a reason in the permissive-omissions map. `CreateResultOut.title`: only the CLI's `create --output json` emits it (`_commands/composer.py:481`); every MCP create tool returns `rebar.create_ticket(return_alias=True)`, which drops title — declaring it would advertise a permanently-null title on a ticket that always has one. `NextBatchOut.tasks`: belongs to the CLI-only `next-batch --limit=0` reduced variant (`_engine_support/next_batch.py:559`); the library/MCP path emits `batch` and never `tasks`.
- **AC4** — wire-contract impact assessed and recorded in a comment on this ticket. **All 39 newly declared fields were ALREADY on the wire** as undeclared `extra="allow"` pass-throughs, verified against this store's real tickets plus a union over 200 closed ones, so the change DOCUMENTS AN EXISTING SHAPE rather than altering what clients receive. That is a materially lower risk profile than F5 assumed when it deferred them.

Hazard surfaced and handled during implementation: declaring an optional pydantic field makes it EMIT, and 15 of the properties have canonical types admitting no null, so a naive declaration made real payloads violate their own schema (8 contract tests caught it). A new `_OmitUnsetOut` base pops never-set fields at serialization, so the declaration appears in `outputSchema` while the emitted bytes are unchanged. Timestamps are typed `int | str | None` rather than bare `int`, because `js_safe_result` would otherwise coerce them to a lossy number on FastMCP re-validation (bug 6fe7).
